owner: CC owns the charter corrections and the gate check. Akien owns the question of whether an at-rest component's absent journal is a red at all, or the ordinary state of a component between voyages

questions.a: THE FILES ARE NOT THE DEFECT; THE SENTENCE IS. Seven missing journals at seven components that have never crossed is the correct state of the world. The charter describing that world wrongly is the only thing here that is broken, and the fix that creates files to match the prose would destroy the honest state to preserve the dishonest description.

THE MECHANISM IS WRONG, NOT JUST THE TENSE. 'Born at the carve-out' is not a true sentence waiting for its files — no journal has ever been born at a carve-out. orient's was born at its first crossing, weeks later, and that is the mechanism for all eight. Correcting only the tense ('will sit beside this charter') would leave the reader with a wrong model of when to expect the record.

HOW SEVEN CHARTERS CAME TO SAY THE SAME FALSE THING: each was written by copying a sibling. This is the same propagation already recorded at n=13 in the memory store — a wrong sentence in a charter is the template the next one is written from — and it is the reason half (2) is a gate check rather than seven edits. Seven edits fix the sample; the check fixes the mechanism.

WHY THIS DID NOT SURFACE UNTIL A TICKET CROSSED. The claim was unfalsifiable in practice: nothing read it, nothing derived it, and a reader who noticed the missing file had no way to tell it from a component between voyages. It surfaced only because orient's journal was BORN today and the contrast made the other seven legible — which is Law 9's shape exactly, a lot turning green one inspected piece at a time and the uninspected ones reading as whatever they last said about themselves.

SCOPE, and it was written into the wrong field at cast — moved here verbatim on 2026-08-14 when test_chart_notes redded it: 'The eight chart machines are where it was measured; the gate check is corpus-wide by construction and will find whatever else asserts a file beside itself. Expect it to red more than these seven on first run — that is the check working, and triaging its first harvest belongs to this ticket, not to a follow-on.' It was filed under chart_notes.scope, and `scope` is not a leg of the chart chain, so it was a note addressed to nobody. THE MOVE IS THE DISPOSITION THE NEW RULE NAMES: a deterministic red is fixed or carries a ruling, and the fix here is to put the prose where it is read rather than to loosen the leg check.

watchme: none, because the enforcement IS the standing instrument and a probe would be a second implementation of the same predicate — the re-derivation Law 1 refuses. After half (2) the sieve fires at every PROVEME crossing (cairn/machines/build_inspector/), so a charter that regains the defect reds a real voyage rather than a watch's counter. REFERENTS: bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate for the hand-run surface, and the PROVEME entry in cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/history.json, whose sieve count lets a reader confirm the new sieve joined. NOT COVERED, stated rather than hidden: between this cast and half (2) landing, nothing watches — a window bounded by the horizon, which is why the horizon is a build-order position and not a date.
dependencies: MEASURED, not assumed: the derivation gate already walks all 54 charters and already proves eight checks over them (bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate), so the ninth check needs no new traversal and no new reader — it needs a predicate. build_inspector already ran 20 sieves over orient at this morning's crossing, so the sieve side needs no new firing path either.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: nothing fires bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate automatically — it is hand-run. That is why half (2) lands as a sieve and not only as a gate check; a corpus check nobody runs is policy wearing a gate's clothes, which is the exact shape Law 4 calls an IOU.

OPEN, and Akien's: does an at-rest component's absent journal red at all? A component that has never sailed HAS no history, and that is its ordinary resting state, not a defect. This ticket's check therefore reds the CHARTER'S CLAIM, never the absence itself — but if the answer is that every component must have crossed at least once, the check is a different one and it is his to name.
filed_edges: verdict's charter says something slightly different from the other six — it adds that the LEDGER is runtime state and lives in instance-space, never here. That clause is TRUE and must survive the correction; the fix is not a blanket replacement across seven files.

The same copy-from-a-sibling propagation almost certainly put other false present-tense claims in charters across the corpus. This ticket does not go looking for them by hand — the gate check is the instrument that finds them, which is why the check is half the ticket and not a nicety.
